newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products perk up despite high freight rate.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products perk up despite high freight rate.

text.p: Med oil products perked up on Thursday despite being limited by high freight rates.
Gasoline prices held steady as healthy demand from the eastern Med and U.S. continued to balance the high freight.
"The arb (to the U.S.) is still open it's just that there are no ships," said one trader.
"For the first half of February there is still good demand...This is as good as the Med gets," he said, noting demand from Turkey and Lebanon.
End-user demand buoyed naphtha prices but the freight rates limited deals getting done.
Gas oil returned to life after several days in the doldrums caused by an acute shipping shortage. But premiums were softer, in part a reflection of high freight rates.

A cargo of Russian 0.2 traded at high cif quotes flat basis Genoa, an Algerian low sulphur diesel traded into Genoa at around cif high flat, and a combination 25,000 tonne cargo of heating oil and low sulphur diedsel was done at high fob Med quotes +$1/1.50 basis Santa Panagia Bay.
Outright prices gained $5 in line with stronger futures lifted by bullish U.S. stocks data and technicals.
High sulphur fuel oil cargoes were steady to firmer.

An Italian refiner sold a 20,000 tonne high sulphur cargo, loading in the first three days Feb, to a trader at around 50-75 cents over the quoted fob high. The cargo was thought likely to co-load with another, and move into Tunisia.
This follows the sale of another Italian cargo on Wednesday at around $94 fob Med. February swaps recovered a couple of dollars and ended around $96/$97 fob.
But the Med remains stronger than the north, and dealers felt more product may head southwards into the region.
Low sulphur markets were steady to firmer. A deal, not confirmed, was heard struck in NWE at around $106 fob.
